To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

• A logic for capabilities is introduced in which not only the knowledge and actions, but also the capabilities of an agent are expressed; • The semantics of this language is given in terms of extended Kripke structures; •
the logic of capabilities is an extension of the logic of knowledge and actions, and that the abilities are closed under equivalence transformations.
we have introduced a logic of capabilities, and that the Can-predicate, and the Cannot-predicates, are definable in this logic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) How can we model abilities? (2) What is the difference between abilities and actions? (3) What is the relationship between knowledge and abilities?
a formalization of capabilities and their relation to knowledge and actions.
the question how the abilities of an intelligent agent can be represented.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the logic of capabilities is a useful tool to reason about the knowledge and the abilities of agents.
a logic of capabilities can be defined, which can be used to reason about knowledge, actions and abilities of agents.
the logic of capabilities is a powerful tool to express and reason about the abilities of an autonomous agent in a dynamic and complex environment.

we have developed a logic of abilities, which is a logic of capabilities.
the proposed framework is able to model the abilities of an autonomous agent in an expressive and flexible way.
we have developed a logic in which not only the knowledge and actions of the agents can be expressed and reasoned with, but also the capabilities of the agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the abilities of agents should be considered in a more general way than is usually done in the literature.
